handbook-text:
Conquest VS Tweaks & Compatibility
Tune the Conquest look, and fix it up alongside other mods

This companion mod adds a green-selective "vibrancy" dial for toning down foliage, and applies compatibility fixes for supported mods when they're detected. Out of the box it changes nothing about how Conquest looks — the vibrancy dial is off until you turn it on. Changes are baked in when the world loads, so edit a setting, then relog to see it.

Commands (type in chat; mind the leading period)
• .ctc list — show the current vibrancy settings and which compatibility fixes are active.
• .ctc vibrancy [0..1] — green saturation multiplier: 1.0 leaves it unchanged, ~0.8 is a gentle knock-down, ~0.6 is stronger, 0.1 is nearly grey. Setting a value turns the dial on.
• .ctc scan — list any blocks rendering the pink/black placeholder and write a report.
• .ctc slabfix [on|off] — toggle the Terrain Slabs connected-texture fix (see below); with no argument, reports the current state. Relog to apply.

Vibrancy dial
Desaturates only the green of the plant tint, leaving dry, brown and autumn tones alone. The game tints grass, ferns, bushes and tree leaves from the same colormap, so this tones down all foliage green together. It's off by default; run .ctc vibrancy 0.8 for a gentle start.

Config file
Everything the commands change — plus advanced hue-band and brightness knobs — lives in ModConfig/conquesttweaks.json.

Compatibility fixes
When a supported mod is detected, its fix activates automatically — no setup. Run .ctc list to see which fixes are active. Currently supported:
• Visible Ores & Minerals — repairs the 3D ore veins that would otherwise show the pink/black placeholder.
• Terrain Slabs — makes Conquest's connected textures line up on slabs (the game otherwise picks a random tile for slab-shaped blocks). Toggle with .ctc slabfix on|off (or EnableSlabsFix in the config); relog to apply.

Advanced: revert individual surfaces to vanilla
If you love most of Conquest but want a few surfaces back to the base-game look, you can revert them one family at a time — soil, grass cover, forest floor, peat, clay, farmland, cob, rammed earth, mud brick, stone path, tall grass and other foliage. This is off by default and takes one setup step, because the mod ships no base-game art.

1. Build the payload (once). Run .ctc reverts extract. This reads your own game files and your installed Conquest pack, and writes the matching vanilla textures into a small pack at Mods/conquesttweaks-vanilla. Nothing is downloaded and nothing leaves your machine — it only copies textures you already own. Relaunch the game afterwards so the pack loads.

2. Turn on the families you want. After relaunching, run .ctc set <family> vanilla (for example .ctc set soil vanilla), then relog to apply. Switch back any time with .ctc set <family> conquest. Run .ctc list to see every family and its current source.

To undo everything, delete the Mods/conquesttweaks-vanilla folder. Note this covers soil and plant surfaces only: stone, gravel, sand, cobblestone, drystone and ore use Conquest's connected-texture grids and can't be reverted this way.
